title: Affirm is Appreciated By Consumers and Merchants as it Facilitates Sales
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkev Tatavosianc revisits Affirm, the buy-now-pay-later lender, after interest rates moved higher. Revenue has grown from $250M in 2020 to $4B over the trailing 12 months, operating-cash-flow-to-sales is at a record high, and revenue per employee has nearly tripled to $1.7M, helped by AI. He argues consumer balance sheets are healthy — unlike before the financial crisis, the excess borrowing this cycle sits with governments, which is where his macro concern lies. On valuation, Affirm at $74 and 14.8x forward earnings looks slightly undervalued overall, though his DCF fair value of $73.16 says fairly valued. He reiterates his late-August BUY ranking but downgrades conviction from medium to low because the valuation is less attractive and rates and macro conditions have worsened.

calls.video_title: Affirm is Appreciated By Consumers and Merchants as it Facilitates Sales
calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (first tracked call) but conviction downgraded medium→low: fairly valued on DCF, slightly undervalued overall at 14.8x forward earnings; rates and macro are worse than at his late-August buy ranking.
calls.base_case: BNPL virtuous cycle (merchants attract consumers and vice versa): revenue $250M in 2020 → $4B TTM, record operating-cash-flow/sales, revenue per employee $1.7M; consumer balance sheets are healthy, unlike pre-GFC.
calls.bull_case: Merchant-network expansion compounds adoption in an industry that could reach billions of customers; AI keeps lifting employee productivity.
calls.bear_case: Fallout from excess government borrowing, higher interest rates and a macro slowdown; valuation less attractive than a month and a half ago.
